message.content:
<summary>
Turn 1: Agent checked /root/input.pptx exists; discovered “python” command missing.  
Turn 2–3: Confirmed python3 is available; no preexisting OOXML helper scripts found.  
Turn 4–5: Tried to use unzip but it wasn’t installed; attempted apt-get install unzip/zip but lacked permissions (cannot acquire apt lock).  
Turn 6: Used python3 zipfile to inspect PPTX (40 entries) and found one embedded Excel workbook at ppt/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx.  
Turn 7: Extracted that embedded workbook to /root/work/embedded.xlsx (10,206 bytes).  
Turn 8: Verified openpyxl is installed.  
Turn 9–10: Located the slide relationship referencing the embedding: ppt/slides/_rels/slide1.xml.rels contains target embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx (not the full ppt/ path).  
Turn 11: Loaded embedded.xlsx with openpyxl and printed the table (Sheet1, max 6x5). Table headers: CNY, USD, EUR, GBP with rows CNY/USD/EUR/GBP. Several cells are formulas like =ROUND(1/B3,3), etc. The hardcoded USD→CNY value is in cell B3 (7.25).  
Turn 12: Parsed all text runs from slide1.xml and found the adjacent text box content: “Updated rate:” and “USD to CNY=7.02”.  
Turn 13–14: Noted there is a preview image ppt/media/image1.emf and slide1.xml contains an OLE object referencing rId2 (embed) and a fallback pic referencing rId3 (image).  
Turn 15: Script parsed the updated rate (USD -> CNY = 7.02), loaded the embedded workbook from the PPTX, mapped currency headers to row/column indices, and updated USD→CNY at B3 from 7.25 to 7.02 (a non-formula cell). It preserved formula cells by only changing the literal value cell. Repacked a new PPTX by copying all original entries and replacing only ppt/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx, saving as /root/results.pptx. Verification re-opened the new PPTX and confirmed the USD→CNY cell now equals 7.02.</summary>

I extracted the embeddings, read the table, parsed the slide textbox, and updated the workbook cell without altering the existing formulas. The results were written to results.pptx by replacing the embeddings. I verified the new value, but I might need to check the potential preview image issue later.
